uncertain.reasoning: This protein is a PurR-family repressor with documented hypoxanthine binding sites and a SITE annotation noting "6-oxopurine corepressor specificity," suggesting capacity to bind guanine. However, experimental evidence explicitly documents only hypoxanthine, not guanine, and these purines are chemically distinct.
HGPRT catalyzes guanine-to-GMP conversion; this protein has a substantial GMP-binding pocket at 133-142, but explicit annotations show GMP (product) binding, not free guanine (substrate) binding.
